title: Commissioning a New Site
contentStatus: Built per Content Principles (60% pass, terminology + notes). Capstone module for L3B, synthesizing map building, mission programming, and FANUC integration (per CDD). New module - does not exist in DiFacto's original slide deck. Facility-specific commissioning checklist pending DiFacto operations input.

sections.title: The Capstone of the Programmer Track
learningObjectives: Understand how this module synthesizes the full L3B skill set
Recognize commissioning as the real-world task L3B-certified programmers perform most often
sections.content: Every module in L3B built toward a single real-world capability: bringing a new MoRo deployment online at a facility that has never run it before. This module is that task in full - map building, mission programming, and machine integration, combined into one end-to-end process. It's the most common task a certified Programmer actually performs, which is why it serves as the track's capstone.

keyTerms.note: An industrial robotics manufacturer whose controllers MoRo commonly integrates with via I/O handshake.
MoRo's Human-Machine Interface (HMI) platform, used for fleet monitoring, mission control, and programming.
The process of determining position while simultaneously building a map of the surrounding environment.

sections.title: Pre-Commissioning Assessment
learningObjectives: Understand what needs evaluating before beginning a commissioning process
Recognize site-specific factors that affect commissioning approach
sections.content: Before mapping begins, a new site needs assessment: floor layout and clearances, existing machine positions, network infrastructure for ANT connectivity, and any site-specific safety considerations. This assessment shapes everything that follows - a facility with tight clearances or heavy machine density needs a different commissioning approach than an open floor plan.

sections.title: Building the Initial Map
learningObjectives: Apply the map-building process (from L3B-M2) to a full new-site context
Understand sequencing considerations for a complete facility map
sections.content: Map building at commissioning scale applies the same SLAM-based process covered earlier in the track, but across an entire operational area rather than a test zone. Sequencing matters: mapping during lower-activity periods reduces the chance of transient obstacles (parked equipment, temporary clutter) becoming permanently embedded in the baseline map.

sections.title: Programming the Initial Mission Set
learningObjectives: Understand how to translate facility workflow into an initial set of missions
Recognize the value of starting with core use cases before adding complexity
sections.content: Once the map exists, initial missions should cover the facility's core, highest-value use cases first - not every conceivable task. Starting narrow and validated, then expanding mission complexity once the basics are proven reliable, reduces risk during the most vulnerable phase of a new deployment: the first weeks of live operation.

sections.title: Integrating With Existing Machines
learningObjectives: Apply machine integration principles (from L3B-M4) in a commissioning context
Understand validation steps before go-live for each integration point
sections.content: Where MoRo interfaces with existing equipment (per L3B-M4's FANUC I/O handshake coverage), each integration point needs individual validation before go-live - confirming the handshake sequence works reliably, not just once under ideal conditions, but repeatedly and under realistic operational variation.

sections.title: Go-Live and Handoff
learningObjectives: Understand the transition from commissioning to live operation
Know what documentation and training the operating site needs at handoff
sections.content: Commissioning isn't complete at technical go-live - it includes ensuring the site's operators (L1-L2 certified) understand the specific mission set and configuration now live at their facility, and that documentation of the commissioning decisions (map version, mission logic, integration points) exists for future reference. A commissioning that works technically but leaves the operating team unprepared hasn't actually succeeded.

questions.question: Why does this module serve as the L3B capstone?
options: It's simply the last module numerically
It synthesizes map building, mission programming, and integration into the most common real-world Programmer task
questions.feedback: Correct. Commissioning combines the full L3B skill set into the task Programmers perform most often.

questions.question: What should be assessed before mapping begins at a new site?
options: Floor layout, machine positions, network infrastructure, and safety considerations
questions.feedback: Correct. Pre-commissioning assessment shapes the entire approach that follows.

questions.question: Why is timing (e.g., mapping during lower-activity periods) a consideration?
options: To reduce transient obstacles becoming permanently embedded in the baseline map
Mapping can only occur at night by regulation
questions.feedback: Correct. Mapping timing affects whether temporary clutter gets baked into the permanent map.

questions.question: What's the recommended approach to the initial mission set?
options: Start with core, highest-value use cases, then expand once proven reliable
Skip mission programming and rely on manual control only
questions.feedback: Correct. Starting narrow and validated reduces risk during the most vulnerable early operational period.

questions.question: Is commissioning complete at technical go-live?
options: Yes, once the technical setup works
Only if the client specifically requests documentation
No - it includes operator preparation and documentation handoff
questions.feedback: Correct. A technically working commissioning that leaves the operating team unprepared hasn't fully succeeded.
